subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Galileo's Discovery of Four Worlds
description: A quick win: understand Galileo's Discovery of Four Worlds.

hook.text: In 1610, Galileo pointed his telescope at Jupiter and saw four tiny lights moving around it. They were moons.

buildup.text: He tracked Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto over weeks. Their orbits proved that not everything revolved around Earth.

discovery.text: This was the first evidence that celestial bodies could orbit something other than Earth—a blow to geocentrism.

twist.text: The Catholic Church pressured Galileo to recant. He spent his final years under house arrest for supporting Copernicus.

climax.text: Today Jupiter has 95 known moons. But those first four changed how humanity understood the universe forever.

punchline.text: Four moons through a simple telescope. They toppled Earth from the center of the cosmos.

quiz.question: Why was Galileo's discovery of Jupiter's moons so revolutionary?
options: It proved that celestial bodies could orbit something other than Earth
It was the first evidence that the Sun orbits the Earth
It showed that moons could support life

details.whyItMatters: Galileo's discovery of Jupiter's moons was a turning point in science. It shattered the ancient belief that Earth was the center of all motion and launched the telescopic era of astronomy.
takeaways: Galileo discovered Jupiter's four largest moons in 1610
Proved that objects can orbit bodies other than Earth
Challenged the geocentric model of the universe

faq.question: Why are they called the Galilean moons?
faq.answer: Named after Galileo Galilei who first observed them. He initially called them the 'Medicean Stars' to honor his patrons. The individual names (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto) were suggested by Simon Marius, who claimed independent discovery.

faq.question: Could Galileo see details on the moons?
faq.answer: No. His telescope was rudimentary — about 20x magnification. The moons appeared only as points of light whose positions changed night to night. But that was enough to prove they orbited Jupiter, not Earth. It took centuries and the Voyager missions to reveal their actual surfaces and diversity.
